key_insight: FrontierPhysics moves beyond fixed physics questions toward evaluating AI agents on end-to-end research. Its benchmark contains 56 tasks created by 42 physicists across nine physics domains.
problem_solved: Existing physics benchmarks focus on isolated tasks, fixed questions, or reproducing papers with known solutions, leaving agents’ broader research abilities and research quality under-evaluated.
method: Build tasks from physicists’ own research to reflect authentic scientific challenges.
Cover nine domains spanning theoretical, computational, and experimental physics.
Frame evaluation around end-to-end research, emphasizing research quality alongside correctness; the provided abstract is truncated before further procedural details.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, FrontierPhysics offers a more research-oriented benchmark for assessing physics agents beyond narrow problem-solving. The provided excerpt does not report model performance or experimental findings.
visual_elements: Three prominent counters: 56 tasks, 42 physicists, nine domains.
Comparison diagram: isolated question answering versus end-to-end research.
Three connected icons representing theoretical, computational, and experimental physics.
Two-axis evaluation graphic highlighting correctness and research quality.
paper_title: FrontierPhysics: Evaluating Agents for End-to-End Physics Research
paper_authors: Bingran You, Wenjun Ke, Ria Rosenauer, Bo Liu, Wenbo Chen
